subject: Clarify ownership & export controls for prompts/responses — DPA addendum
messages:
From: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@clearhealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: devon.mckay@clearhealth.com
Date: Sat, 30 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA addendum — prompt/response ownership & exports

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — ClearHealth is excited about the latency profile on the Redwood hosted endpoint. Before we proceed to procurement we need to nail a few data-use items in the DPA addendum so our security and legal teams can sign off. Key asks from our side:

- A clear ownership clause stating that all prompts and model-generated responses submitted by ClearHealth remain our data (no assignment/licensing of PHI-derived outputs).
- A formal no-training/no-model-improvement commitment for any data we send unless explicitly enabled and contracted (we can pay for an opt-in model-improvement program but must default to opt-out).
- Specific retention limits for prompts/outputs (we'd prefer 30 days, then deletion unless retained for billing/audit with explicit notice).
- A subprocessors list and a mechanism for notice/objection before a new subprocessor is engaged.
- Clarification on cross-border transfers (most of our data subjects are in the EU — we need SCCs or equivalent safeguards; also whether data is routed or stored in the US).

Can you share your proposed addendum language and the current subprocessors list? Also please include any windows or SLA impacts if we choose a strict no-training commitment.

Best,
Elaine
Director, Security & Compliance
ClearHealth Systems

From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@clearhealth.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Sep 2025 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA addendum — prompt/response ownership & exports

Hi Elaine,

Really appreciate the clear list. I’ve looped in Naomi (legal) and Marcus (AE) to scope the addendum and make sure we surface any commercial trade-offs. High-level responses for now:

- Ownership: Redwood’s standard position is that customers retain ownership of their inputs and outputs. We can put an explicit ownership clause in the addendum to remove ambiguity.
- No-training default: We offer a default no-training setting for enterprise customers as a configurable control. There is an implementation and cost delta (some throughput optimizations rely on aggregated telemetry); Naomi can propose precise language and an opt-in paid program for model-improvement where customers affirmatively allow retention for training.
- Retention: We can accommodate a 30-day retention for content and then automatic deletion, with the caveat that billing/audit logs may be persisted longer in aggregated/hashed form. We’ll add explicit exceptions and notice requirements.
- Subprocessors: attaching current list and we maintain a 30-day notification window before onboarding a materially new subprocessor. If ClearHealth objects we’ll provide an escalation path.
- Transfers: We'll offer SCCs for EU transactions and can provide an option to pin tenant data to EU-only Dedicated or Private deployments if residency is required. For Hosted, data may transit through US infra for control-plane operations but we can confirm encryption and access controls.

Attached: redwood_dpa_addendum_v1.docx — this is a working draft with placeholders for the ownership and no-training language. Naomi, could you take the lead on suggested redlines?

Next steps: Naomi and I will produce two alternative clauses for the model-improvement opt-in/opt-out and a clear data-residency paragraph. Marcus — can you confirm timeline for procurement so we prioritize the right level of legal review?

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Devon McKay <devon.mckay@clearhealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@clearhealth.com>, anil@legalpartner.com
Date: Tue, 02 Sep 2025 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA addendum — prompt/response ownership & exports

Rishi / Naomi,

Thanks for the quick reply and draft. A couple of follow-ups from our legal team (Anil is on copy):

1) "Ownership" should explicitly state that ClearHealth retains all rights to prompts and responses and that Redwood will not assert any IP or license claim over generated outputs derived from ClearHealth data.

2) "No-training" language needs a one-sentence proof point: that data submitted under the no-training setting will never be used to update any production or research models, nor used to fine-tune any third-party models. We need an auditable statement.

3) Subprocessors: please confirm whether security logs or troubleshooting dumps may be shared with a subprocessor and what minimization rules apply. Also confirm notification cadence (30 days is good; can we get a certified list and a point of contact for objections).

4) Transfers: SCCs are acceptable; please confirm whether any metadata or logs required for billing contain personal data and whether those elements leave the EU. If we cannot guarantee EU-only storage for control-plane logs, we will likely require a Private deployment.

Happy to run the draft through our procurement committee once we have these clarifications. Please let us know if Redwood needs any templated language on our side for the opt-in model-improvement program or if you prefer to draft that.

Regards,
Devon
Sr. Procurement Manager, ClearHealth

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@clearhealth.com>, Devon McKay <devon.mckay@clearhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, anil@legalpartner.com
Date: Tue, 02 Sep 2025 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA addendum — prompt/response ownership & exports

Hi Elaine / Devon / Anil,

Thanks for the concrete asks — attaching redline with proposed language. Below are the key clauses I recommend (extracted from the draft to make review faster):

- Ownership: "Customer Data" means prompts and all model-generated outputs submitted by Customer. Redwood acknowledges and agrees that Customer retains sole ownership of Customer Data. Redwood shall not assert any rights, title, or interest in Customer Data, and shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve any models unless Customer provides an express written opt-in.

- No-Training/Opt-Out: "By default, Customer Data shall not be used to train or improve Redwood models or third-party models. Customers may elect an opt-in model-improvement program under a separate addendum which will include pricing and a data minimization plan." Auditability: Redwood will provide an attestation on request (quarterly) confirming segregation of opt-out traffic and any logs used for operational purposes will be pseudonymized and excluded from training pipelines.

- Retention: "Customer Data will be deleted from primary stores within 30 days after receipt, except where retention is required for billing/audit obligations; any retained material will be pseudonymized and retained only for the minimum period necessary. Control-plane metadata required for billing may be retained for up to 12 months but will be hashed and encrypted at rest."

- Subprocessors: "Redwood shall maintain a current list of subprocessors and post updates to [link]. Redwood shall provide Customer with 30 days' prior notice before engaging a new subprocessor and will provide reasonable information to allow Customer to object. For emergency onboarding of a subprocessor (e.g., critical security patches), Redwood will notify Customer as soon as practicable and provide remediation options."

- Transfers: "Redwood will process EU Personal Data under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (or equivalent), and will offer EU-only data residency options for Dedicated/Private deployments. Control-plane metadata may be routed via US control-plane systems; Redwood will provide encryption and access controls and will identify any personal data contained in such metadata upon request."

If that language looks acceptable I’ll incorporate it into the attached redline (redline_privacy_addendum_v2.docx) and we can move to DocuSign. If ClearHealth wants a binding SOC2 attestation for the opt-out controls, we can scope that as an SLA add-on.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
